text:
Taylor: heads-up — I'm drafting an RFC for schema-degradation and error pathways for structured output / tool-calling. Need to align on acceptance criteria, launch scope, and customer-driven tradeoffs. pinging product + eng.

Maya: +1. Important to capture customer asks like Acme's soft-mode requirement (partial results + warnings) and 403/authz semantics when tool calls hit errors.

Raj: infra note — we need explicit fallback model variants, circuit breaker rules, and clarity on telemetry so we don't lose observability when validators drop outputs. Also call out cost impact on batching.

Carmen: proposal for v1 minimal scope: 1) strict/hard schema validation with clear error codes; 2) deterministic fallback to text-only answer (no tool call); 3) telemetry + sample retention for failed validations. Acceptance criteria: <=1% user-visible schema failures in month 1, SDK exposes fallback header, docs & quickstart.

Kevin: quick question — what do we mean by "deterministic fallback" in practice? example?

Taylor: example payload we expect to return on fallback:

```json
{
  "fallback": "text",
  "reason_code": "schema_invalid",
  "raw_output": "<model raw response>"
}
```

and an HTTP header: `X-Redwood-Fallback: schema-invalid`. This keeps client behavior predictable. We'll need acceptance tests that assert header + structured body shape.

Maya: also need to define soft vs hard validation modes. Soft = return best-effort partial + `warnings` field. Hard = reject and trigger deterministic fallback. Soft is preferred by some customers but is more complex for SDKs.

Raj: operationally, soft mode means more downstream merging logic and larger error surface. Recommend default = hard, opt-in soft via route config (e.g. `?validation_mode=soft` or per-route flag on Dedicated).

Carmen: launch checklist (initial):
- PRD + RFC merged
- docs + SDK example for fallback header
- one pilot customer (Acme or internal)
- regression tests + synthetic harness for common schemas
- perf budget: tail latency +5% max

Kevin: prioritization ask — is this Q2 ship or Q3? we need to balance against cache & batching improvements.

Taylor: proposed roadmap: ship v1 (hard default + telemetry) in next sprint cycle as high priority. v1.1 (soft-mode beta + per-field partial merges) in later cycle. We need PM sign-off to deprioritize per-field merges if resource constrained.

Maya: customer note: Acme has said they will only accept soft-mode. Can we offer soft-mode as a private beta behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers?

Raj: feasible but requires config + rollout + monitoring dashboards. Estimate ~3 engineer-weeks end-to-end (infra + runtime + canary + tests).

Taylor: action items: I'll write PRD + RFC draft tonight. @Maya please add Acme's acceptance criteria and sample prompts. @Raj can you attach cost/effort estimate and minimal infra design? @Carmen can you draft the acceptance checklist so QA has a concrete plan?

product-bot: reminder — RFC draft due in 72 hours. Create PR under `docs/rfcs/` and assign reviewers (product, eng-runtime, eng-ml).

Carmen: 👍 drafting checklist now, will drop link to doc in this thread when ready.

Kevin: +1. If Acme is blocking, let's offer private beta + explicit contract for pilot timelines.

Maya: agree. I'll coordinate with customer success for pilot comms and data retention questions.

Taylor: cool — I'll post RFC link once initial draft is up. Thanks all.
